req.title: Login rejects wrong username
req.statement: The system shall render an 'Incorrect username.' error when the supplied username is not found.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-009 requires that POST /auth/login returns an HTTP 2xx response containing the exact text 'Incorrect username.' when the supplied username does not exist in the database. The violation in test[0] was kind='negative' paired with heuristic='EP': EP is a partitioning technique that can cover both positive and negative partitions, but when the test is explicitly classified as 'negative' the correct heuristic label is 'NEG' (negative testing / error-guessing). Fix: change test[0] heuristic from 'EP' to 'NEG'. All other tests are preserved unchanged. Five tests total: (1) NEG — completely non-existent username triggers 'Incorrect username.'; (2) BVA — one-char-shorter near-miss username; (3) DT — correct username + wrong password fires 'Incorrect password.' not 'Incorrect username.' confirming mutual exclusivity; (4) BVA — empty-string username at zero-length boundary; (5) NEG — case-sensitive mismatch ('james' vs 'James'). Together these kill mutations that swap error strings, negate the user-is-None check, or merge the two error branches.

tests.name: test_login_wrong_username_shows_incorrect_username_error
preconditions: Database contains users: Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, Diya, James (ids 1-5)
Username 'NoSuchUser' does not exist in the database
expected: Response body does NOT contain 'Incorrect password.'
trace: R-FLASKR-009: system shall render 'Incorrect username.' when username not found
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'NoSuchUser', 'password': 'anypassword'})
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Incorrect username.' in r.data
assert b'Incorrect password.' not in r.data

preconditions: Database contains user 'James' (id=5); 'james' (all lowercase) does not exist
expected: Response body does NOT contain 'Incorrect password.'
trace: R-FLASKR-009: username lookup is case-sensitive; 'james' != 'James' so user is None and 'Incorrect username.' must appear
